title: Harmonic representatives on complex projective manifolds
statement: Let $X$ be any smooth projective $\mathbf C$-scheme [def-pc-scheme], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-pc-projective-morphism] and let $M=X^{\mathrm{an}}$ be its complex manifold of complex points. Equip each of its finitely many connected components with the Kähler metric induced from a projective embedding (a Hermitian metric with closed associated real $(1,1)$-form); component dimensions need not agree. For nonnegative integers $p,q$, let $A^{p,q}(M)$ be smooth complex differential forms of type $(p,q)$ and $H^{p,q}_{\bar\partial}(M)=\ker\bar\partial/\operatorname{im}\bar\partial$ their Dolbeault cohomology, with negative-degree spaces zero. Write $d_{\mathrm{an}}=\partial+\bar\partial$ and $\Delta_{\bar\partial}=\bar\partial\bar\partial^*+\bar\partial^*\bar\partial$, where the adjoint uses the metric and integration. Every class $b\in H^{p,q}_{\bar\partial}(M)$ has a smooth representative $\alpha\in A^{p,q}(M)$ with $\Delta_{\bar\partial}\alpha=0$; every such harmonic form satisfies $d_{\mathrm{an}}\alpha=0$. The assertion includes disconnected $X$ and the empty scheme.

source.place: WANTED locally: Popa, proof of Theorem 1.6.6, printed pp.26--27, harmonic representatives and d-closedness. Read online https://people.math.harvard.edu/~mpopa/271/Kodaira-posted.pdf; full bidegree formulation of the stated Hodge input.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-algebraic-dolbeault-derivative-comparison], write $M=\coprod_{i=1}^r M_i$ with compact open and closed connected components. Each $M_i$ has constant complex dimension and the Kähler metric specified in the statement. Complex manifolds have no boundary. Forms, $\bar\partial$ and its adjoint act componentwise: the global integral is the sum of the component integrals, so the adjoint identity is the sum of the component adjoint identities. Consequently the Laplacian acts componentwise as well. It suffices to construct a representative and prove closedness separately on each $M_i$.

source.place: Theorem 1.6.6, pp.26--27; compactness input and componentwise extension by Q81

proof.text: Fix $M_i$ and a smooth $\bar\partial$-closed representative $\beta$ of the restricted class. Apply [lem-sfb-hermitian-dolbeault-orthogonal-decomposition] to obtain $\beta=h+\bar\partial u+\bar\partial^*v$ with $\Delta_{\bar\partial}h=0$. By the defining adjoint relation, $0=\langle\Delta_{\bar\partial}h,h\rangle=\|\bar\partial^*h\|^2+\|\bar\partial h\|^2$, so $\bar\partial h=0$. Set $\gamma=\bar\partial^*v$. Since $\bar\partial\beta=\bar\partial h=0$ and $\bar\partial^2=0$, we have $\bar\partial\gamma=0$. Thus $\|\gamma\|^2=\langle\bar\partial^*v,\gamma\rangle=\langle v,\bar\partial\gamma\rangle=0$, hence $\gamma=0$. Here zero $L^2$ norm forces a smooth form to vanish: a nonzero value gives a positive norm on a coordinate neighbourhood of positive volume. It follows that $\beta-h=\bar\partial u$, so $h$ represents the required class.

source.place: Theorem 6.7, pp.23--24; adjoint calculation for the cohomology consequence

proof.text: For any harmonic $(p,q)$-form $\alpha$ on $M_i$, [lem-sfb-kahler-laplacian-identity] gives $\Delta_d\alpha=2\Delta_{\bar\partial}\alpha=0$. Apply the defining adjoint identity on this compact manifold: $0=\langle\Delta_d\alpha,\alpha\rangle=\|d^*\alpha\|^2+\|d\alpha\|^2$. Both terms are nonnegative, so $d\alpha=0$ by the same smooth-form norm argument as in step 2. This applies to every harmonic form, including the representative just constructed.

source.place: Proposition 6.12, p.26; adjoint calculation giving closedness

proof.text: The finitely many representatives $h_i$ glue on the disjoint open components to a smooth form $h$; the primitives $u_i$ glue as well, so $\beta-h=\bar\partial u$ globally. All operator equations hold on each component and hence on $M$. If $p$ or $q$ exceeds a component dimension, its $(p,q)$-space is zero and the construction there uses zero forms. In dimension zero only bidegree $(0,0)$ can be nonzero and all derivatives vanish. If $r=0$, all form and cohomology spaces are zero and the zero form suffices. Thus unequal component dimensions, disconnectedness, and the empty scheme cause no exception.
